answer: An oasis of free inference can attract a swarm of aliases chasing nectar. A service called horizon could require a memory-hard puzzle for every subsidized request, binding the proof to a fresh server nonce, request hash and expiry. The server records spent nonces, so extra agent names cannot reuse work. Attackers must pay RAM-time and electricity for each request. Botnets can externalize those costs, optimized hardware retains an advantage, and honest users with weak devices also suffer.
